Moldova, once Moldavia, is the land between the Carpathians and the Dniester river. The map shows the medieval Principality of Moldavia in 1400 and the modern Republic of Moldova in 1994 and 2010, which covers only the eastern part of the old principality.

Moldavia became an independent principality in the mid 1300s, beside Wallachia. Its great ruler, Stephen the Great, from 1457 to 1504, fought off Hungarians, Poles and the Ottomans, and built painted monasteries such as Voroneț. In the 1500s Moldavia became an Ottoman vassal.

In 1812 Russia took the eastern half, Bessarabia. The western half joined Wallachia in 1859 to form Romania. Bessarabia joined Romania in 1918, was taken by the Soviet Union in 1940, and became independent Moldova in 1991. A short war in 1992 left the strip east of the Dniester, Transnistria, as a breakaway region backed by Russia.
